concepts.tradeoffs:
POWER vs. COGNITIVE LOAD:
  - Dense 3-column layout is optimized for speed and information discovery at the cost of initial overwhelm.
  - Mitigated by: first-visit animation tour, keyboard shortcuts in tooltips, command palette hiding complexity.
  - Progressive users (2+ completed projects) are the target; new users stay in standard ProgressiveFlow.

ALWAYS-VISIBLE STATE vs. FOCUS:
  - Watch-list continuously shows risks/assumptions can split attention away from the step itself.
  - Mitigated by: right-dock fullscreen mode (cmd+r toggles, hides center watch-list). Power users can work in either mode.

KEYBOARD-FIRST vs. DISCOVERABILITY:
  - Shortcuts are powerful but hidden. Users who don't know cmd+k won't find them.
  - Mitigated by: first-time tutorial, "?" help button always visible, tooltips on hover, keyboard hints in tabs.

BRANCH COMPLEXITY:
  - Multi-branch navigation adds cognitive overhead if users have 10+ branches.
  - Mitigated by: fuzzy search + fuzzy jump-to (cmd+j filters by checkpoint headline), branches sorted by recency, color coding.

MOBILE UX SACRIFICE:
  - 3-column layout collapses to drawer + fullscreen. Swiping to reveal log/dock is less discoverable than tabs.
  - This is intentional: Command Deck is "desktop power user" interface. Mobile users stay in ProgressiveFlow layout.

STREAMING REAL-TIME UPDATES:
  - Watch-list updating during LLM streaming can cause layout jank if assumptions/risks re-order frequently.
  - Mitigated by: use CSS Grid with fixed row heights + animate-in-place transitions (don't remount), virtualize if >10 items.

INFORMATION DENSITY vs. SCROLLING:
  - Left rail, center, and right dock all scroll independently. Users must manage 3 scroll contexts.
  - Mitigated by: left rail is sticky (always see current waypoint); cmd+j jumps; right dock action buttons are sticky.

ASSUMPTION/RISK LIFECYCLE:
  - Clicking assumptions/risks to expand is a discovered interaction. Many users will miss it.
  - Mitigated by: tooltip on first hover, animated pulse on new unresolved items, "hover to see details" hint.

DIVERGENCE FROM "VOYAGE CALM":
  - Dense cockpit aesthetic is busier than the serene, "empty screen" design philosophy.
  - This is intentional design divergence for this surface: the angle is "power user cockpit," not "calm harbor."
  - Mitigated by: color palette stays warm (gold/cream), generous whitespace between sections, slow spring transitions preserve the voyage mood.

scores.judge_lens: Target-user value for a NON-DEVELOPER STRATEGIST whose real alternative is 'just ask ChatGPT directly.' I score how fast and how genuinely each concept delivers the five DNA 'moments' (esp. #1 'that's my real problem' and #3 'this stakeholder will stab here'), and whether it earns the next use. I am skeptical of cleverness — spatial dexterity, keyboard chords, and chart-reading skill are DEVELOPER pleasures, not strategist value. A strategist wants: low cognitive load, the context-chain made visibly trustworthy ('the AI actually carried my reframe forward'), and a calm pace that makes thinking feel supported. The harness's whole pitch is 'slow down before you recast' — so an interface that rewards focus beats one that rewards speed/density.

rankings.concept_name: Calming Full-Screen Canvas: Each Voyage Step as a Dedicated, Centered Stage
rankings.note: Directly serves the non-dev strategist. One question per screen IS the §3.1 'calm near-empty screen, one question at center' philosophy made literal, and the AnchoringMoment + ContextCarryToast operationalize §3.2 (맥락 누적을 눈으로 확인) better than any competitor — the toast '← From your reframe: X' is the single most legible proof that 'the AI carried my thinking forward,' which is exactly what beats raw ChatGPT. VoyageGuide's collapsible previous-step summaries give trust without demanding chart-reading. Pacing (anchoring ritual, no auto-progression) embodies 'think before you recast' as a felt experience, not a slogan. Feasibility 4 not 5: refactoring the 2670-line ProgressiveFlow is real work and disabling lateral jump/branching removes existing capability (mitigated by their Express Mode escape hatch). Honest risk: forced linearity could chafe returning users, and deferring all outputs to a 'Delivery Hall' delays the moment-of-value — but for a FIRST-time strategist deciding what to have AI do, the calm wins. Time-to-genuine-value is fastest here because nothing competes for attention.

rankings.concept_name: Navigable Voyage Atlas — The Interactive Nautical Chart as Decision Theater
rankings.note: Gorgeous and the most literal expression of the voyage metaphor, but it optimizes for a strategist who thinks spatially and enjoys interrogating a map — a minority. For the median non-dev under time pressure, a 3-column legend/chart/manifest with toggleable assumption-diamond / risk-heatmap / ancestry-thread overlays is COGNITIVE LOAD, not value; it asks them to learn a chart literacy before getting their answer, which plays into ChatGPT's 'just ask me' advantage. The exportable PNG 'decision artifact' is genuinely good (honors §1.3 해도 자체가 지식) and is the strongest single idea here. Feasibility 2: this is the heaviest build — pan/zoom hit-detection, responsive overlay layers, a ~400-line interactive ChartVoyage replacing the static one, AND it specs html2canvas which is NOT in package.json (export.ts has no canvas pipeline). Philosophy 4: faithful to mood/metaphor but flirts with the 'AI-dashboard density' the philosophy explicitly avoids. Value lands mostly at the END (reviewing a finished voyage), not during the thinking — so it earns re-use as a portfolio/share artifact more than as a first-run experience.

rankings.concept_name: Command Deck: The Argus Fast-Track Workspace
rankings.note: Self-admittedly diverges from 'voyage calm' for a 'desktop power-user cockpit' — and the target user is explicitly a NON-developer strategist, the population least served by cmd+k, cmd+1-5 chords, a debugger-style watch-list, and three independent scroll contexts. This is built for the judge's own profession, not the buyer's. The always-visible context-origin tags ('← from 항로 재설정', '← assumption #3 unresolved') are a real asset and the strongest grafting candidate. But density actively undermines the product's core thesis ('slow down before you recast') — it rewards velocity, which is the exact failure mode (첫 세이렌에게 뛰어들기) Argus exists to prevent. Gated behind 2+ completed projects, so it can't be the primary IA. Feasibility 2: new CommandDeck/ subtree, keyboard hook, dual-layout routing, real-time streaming-into-watch-list jank risk. Lowest target-user value because a strategist gets MORE confused, not less, and gains nothing ChatGPT doesn't already give them (speed).

scores.best_concept: Calming Full-Screen Canvas: Each Voyage Step as a Dedicated, Centered Stage
best_ideas_worth_grafting: From Atlas: the exportable voyage chart as a high-res PNG 'decision artifact' — bind it to the existing BranchMap/VoyageChart (already 395 lines of SVG) and the Delivery Hall, not a new interactive canvas. Add ONE dependency (html2canvas) only here. This honors §1.3 '해도 자체가 지식' and gives strategists a shareable team document, the thing ChatGPT can't produce.

From Atlas: the convergence compass-rose / 'bearing toward True North' as the visual for refinement convergence_score (assessConvergence already exists in progressive-convergence.ts) — drop it into the focused-linear Step 4 header and its AnchoringMoment ('수렴도: 78% — 한 번 더 항로를 잡아보시겠습니까?'), so the §10 moment #4 gets a calm, single-glyph visual instead of a busy dashboard.

From Command Deck: always-visible context-origin tags ('← from 항로 재설정 Q2', '← assumption #3 unresolved') attached to carried-forward fields. Graft these INTO the VoyageGuide sidebar and ContextCarryToast as inline provenance labels — this is the cheapest, highest-trust way to make the 맥락 누적 체인 (the moat) visible, and it pairs perfectly with the typed ContextChain._source metadata from ROADMAP Phase 0.

From Atlas: assumption verification as a first-class toggle (✓ verified / unresolved) surfaced in the VoyageGuide's 'Key 전제' list rather than buried in prose — directly drives ROADMAP's success metric '평균 전제 확인됨 마킹 수 > 0.5개/세션' and creates moment #1 ('that's my real problem'). Render as a simple list with toggles, NOT as spatial diamonds on a chart.

From Atlas: branch/fork visualization for returning power users — but keep it docked/optional (a right drawer in focused-linear) rather than the central 60% pane, so first-time strategists aren't forced to read a git-graph to get value.

From Command Deck: the cmd+k command palette and keyboard shortcuts as a strictly-optional, hidden power layer (never in the default UI), satisfying returning users without imposing density on first-run strategists — exactly the 'Express Mode / Cmd+2 jump' escape hatch focused-linear already proposed.

scores.judge_lens: Senior design engineer on this exact stack (Next 16, Tailwind v4, Zustand, framer-motion). I score buildability on the CURRENT architecture, quality ceiling, and maintenance cost — penalizing concepts that fight existing primitives (declarative BranchMap/layoutBranchMap, computed branch lineage via getActivePath, the 2670-line ProgressiveFlow, parsePartialAnalysis streaming, the Logbook rail) or introduce uninstalled deps (html2canvas, cmdk).

rankings.concept_name: Command Deck: The Argus Fast-Track Workspace
rankings.note: Most architecturally honest of the three. It lives in a NEW src/components/workspace/CommandDeck/ dir behind a layoutPreference flag (progressive | command-deck), leaving the 2670-line ProgressiveFlow and all tests (1004 pass) untouched — zero blast radius, opt-in for 2+ project veterans. The center watch-list reuses parsePartialAnalysis (already streaming today) and the left spine reuses checkpoints/waypoints/branches + navigateToCheckpoint/switchBranch verbatim. cmdk is NOT installed but a hotkey hook (useCommandDeckKeyboard) + a hand-rolled palette is ~1 day, no dep. CRAFT RISK: 3-column independent-scroll layout with live re-ordering watch-list is real jank territory (concept correctly flags fixed-row CSS grid mitigation). FIDELITY is the weak axis: dense cockpit explicitly diverges from '동틀 녘의 항구' calm-harbor DNA — author owns this as intentional, scoped to power users, palette stays warm/gold. For a NON-DEV strategist (the stated target), cmd+k/cmd+1-5 ceremony adds learning cost without proportional decision value; this is a returning-power-user surface, not the core value path.

rankings.concept_name: Navigable Voyage Atlas — The Interactive Nautical Chart as Decision Theater
rankings.note: Highest fidelity — it makes '맥락 누적 체인' literally visible (ancestry threads), which is the product's deepest promise, and the graticule/gold-thread/navy-node palette is dead-on the mood board. But the concrete_spec FIGHTS the architecture in three concrete ways. (1) It proposes an imperative lib/voyage-chart-renderer.ts that builds SVG via createElementNS and addEventListener — the codebase already renders the chart DECLARATIVELY via BranchMap.tsx + pure layoutBranchMap(); the spec would fork or replace that, doubling maintenance. (2) It reads cp.x/cp.y and cp.branch_id off checkpoints, but types.ts deliberately does NOT store branch_id (comment: 'a single owner id would be a lie and a future consistency bug' — lineage is computed via getActivePath), and coords come from layoutBranchMap, not the store. (3) hidden_assumptions/classified_risks are NOT flat per-checkpoint fields; they're nested in state_snapshot.snapshots and dm_feedback, so 'classified_risks_by_checkpoint' needs a real derivation selector. (4) exportChartAsPNG calls html2canvas — uninstalled, and html2canvas can't rasterize var(--…) custom-prop fills reliably; you'd need a native SVG-serialize→canvas path. Pan/zoom + hit-detection + responsive diamond layering is the ~400-line component the author admits. Buildable, but it's a 4-5 week rebuild of a surface that already works, with a higher maintenance ceiling. Best as an EVOLUTION of VoyageChart, not a from-scratch renderer.

rankings.concept_name: Calming Full-Screen Canvas: Each Voyage Step as a Dedicated, Centered Stage
rankings.note: Strongest fit to Philosophy §3 (calm, one-thing-at-a-time, narrated context carry-forward) and §10 moments, and the anchoring-moment ritual is genuinely on-brand. Real value for a first-time non-dev. BUT craft cost is the highest and most dangerous: it explicitly refactors the 2670-line ProgressiveFlow, which today is not a clean step-carousel — it inlines worker deployment, the Logbook, forking, verification gates, and streaming. The concept DEFERS forking to a drawer and DISABLES lateral 'jump to step 3' navigation that the Logbook/VoyageChart already provide — i.e. it removes shipped capability, and would break/rewrite flow-interactions.test, logbook-render tests, etc. STEPS metadata is reused (good), EASE token exists (good), but '2-3 weeks' is optimistic given the test surface and the worker/branch concerns that don't fit a linear 4-act model. AnchoringMoment/VoyageGuide/ContextCarryToast are clean new components, but they sit on top of a load-bearing refactor. The deferred Delivery Hall (outputs only after step 4) also regresses today's inline-output access. High quality ceiling IF rebuilt, but the architecture-fighting penalty is severe.

scores.best_concept: Command Deck: The Argus Fast-Track Workspace
best_ideas_worth_grafting: From Atlas: ancestry/context-chain threads as a TOGGLEABLE OVERLAY inside the EXISTING declarative BranchMap.tsx (add an optional <path stroke=var(--accent) dasharray> layer keyed off getActivePath + stage lineage) — delivers the highest-fidelity 'context made visible' move WITHOUT the imperative renderer rewrite or html2canvas. This is the single most valuable graft.

From Atlas: a per-checkpoint derivation SELECTOR (deriveAssumptionsForCheckpoint / deriveRisksForCheckpoint reading state_snapshot.snapshots + dm_feedback) — useful to ANY concept that wants to surface assumption/risk status on the chart or rail, and honors the 'lineage is computed, not stored' rule.

From Atlas: the convergence compass-rose micro-indicator (rotate by convergence_score, which already exists at types.ts:709) as a small header glyph — a cheap, on-brand replacement for a generic progress bar; addable to the Logbook header today.

From Focused-Linear: the AnchoringMoment step-exit ritual card and explicit 'context carry-forward' narration ('← From your reframe: X') — these are pure-additive components that can drop into the EXISTING ProgressiveFlow phase transitions without the full-screen refactor, capturing the calm-ceremony DNA Command Deck lacks.

From Focused-Linear: the VoyageGuide sidebar's read-only 'original problem + current step purpose + collapsed previous-step summaries' — graft into the existing right-rail Logbook as a top section, giving Command Deck's dense cockpit a calmer anchor and softening its DNA divergence.

From Command Deck: explicit context-origin tags ('← from 항로 재설정', '← assumption #3 unresolved') on rendered items — a low-cost traceability pattern that strengthens the context-chain story across all surfaces.

From Command Deck: gate any cockpit/power surface behind layoutPreference in useWorkspaceStore so the calm default (HeroFlow → ProgressiveFlow) is preserved for new non-dev users — adopt this opt-in pattern for ANY ambitious surface so the 1004-test baseline and the calm-harbor default stay intact.

scores.judge_lens: Philosophy-fidelity guardian of the voyage DNA. I score truth to metaphor-as-function so the nautical word IS the function, section 3 calm near-empty screen and one-thing-at-a-time and context carry-forward made visible, section 6 dawn-harbor mood of warm ivory and gold editorial serif generous whitespace slow spring while avoiding generic AI-dashboard and cold tech-blue and purple gradients and dense cockpits, and whether it manufactures the 5 moments. I penalize generic-AI drift because the moat is the calm judgment-first feel a dashboard destroys.
best_ideas_worth_grafting: Atlas ancestry thread: a thin gold dashed curve from the current stage node back to its prior-stage source, rendering the context-accumulation chain (the section 2.2 moat) as a literally traceable line. Graft into the focused-linear voyage guide; the existing static SVG BranchMap can draw one extra dashed path with zero new dependencies.

Atlas chart-as-artifact (section 1.3, the chart itself is knowledge): export the voyage trail as a shareable document built on the EXISTING lib/export.ts markdown as a Voyage Log section with the waypoint glyph trail (anchor departure, milestone course-change, reef hazard), NOT an html2canvas PNG which is an absent dependency that cannot cleanly rasterize an SVG transform viewport. The Delivery Hall mockup already drafts this trail; make it the Project Brief headline.

Assumption verification as a visible first-class object. The data already exists in state_snapshot.hidden_assumptions and classified_risks in types.ts. Surface a verified/unverified toggle inside the focused-linear voyage guide previous-step cards so marking a premise confirmed is a calm side-action, without the Atlas diamond-overlay clutter or the Deck debugger watch-list.

Command Deck origin-tagging microcopy (from reframe, from assumption 3). Keep ONLY this traceability label idea to serve section 3.2 see-the-carry-forward-with-your-eyes; attach it to the focused-linear context-carry toast. Discard the cockpit, the command palette, and the watch-list entirely.

One quiet returning-user affordance (section 10 moment 2, now I can see the whole thing): keyboard Back/Next plus an optional Express Mode that skips to step 2 when a reframe already exists. Adopt as restrained shortcuts only; reject the always-visible dense cockpit that surfaced them.

Correction to graft into the winner: re-tone the focused-linear per-step header accents 2d4a7c blue and 6b4c9a purple, which violate the section 6 ban on cold tech-blue and purple. Map all four steps to the warm navy/charcoal and gold/amber family; reserve risk-purple 7F77DD for the rehearse risk context only, never as step chrome.

rankings.concept_name: Calming Full-Screen Canvas: Each Voyage Step as a Dedicated, Centered Stage
rankings.note: The philosophy made literal. Maps one-to-one to 3.1 calm one-question screen, 3.2 transition messages narrating context carry-forward (its copy nearly quotes the doc), 3.3 the context-carry toast, and 3.4 plus section 10 the Anchoring Moment as the ship-bell ceremony, the breath between legs. Every nautical word stays function-bound and paired with the work term. Manufactures moments 1 2 4 directly and stages 5 via Delivery Hall. Feasibility 4 not 5: restructures the 2670-line ProgressiveFlow, but the current flow is already a calm centered max-w-2xl column with an lg rail so much is reusable; it does regress the existing logbook lateral-jump and forking. One risk: per-step header accents flirt with the banned cold-blue and purple and must be re-toned to gold and navy. The truest extension of the DNA, not a reinvention.

rankings.concept_name: Navigable Voyage Atlas: The Interactive Nautical Chart as Decision Theater
rankings.note: Strongest single idea in the set: section 1.3 the chart itself is knowledge made literal, and ancestry threads turn the invisible context-accumulation chain into a visible gold line you follow backward, directly serving the stated moat in 2.2. Graticule, gold threads, navy nodes, warm bg honor section 6. But fidelity capped at 4 and value at 3 because the execution drifts toward generic-AI territory: git-graph language and a 3-column legend/chart/manifest layout that fills the screen with panels, the antithesis of section 3 near-empty calm, risking that the non-dev strategist must learn the map before they can think, which violates the cardinal rule that a metaphor you must learn has failed. Feasibility 2 is the blocker: it replaces static SVG BranchMap with pan-zoom plus hit-detection plus 3 overlay layers plus PNG export via html2canvas, which is absent from package.json and cannot cleanly rasterize an SVG transform viewport anyway. A multi-week, 5-phase build with new store state, mobile timeline fallback, and large-graph perf concerns. The export-artifact idea deserves to live; the atlas-as-default does not.

rankings.concept_name: Command Deck: The Argus Fast-Track Workspace
rankings.note: The generic-AI-app drift section 6 explicitly forbids, wearing a nautical skin: a dense 3-column cockpit, a debugger watch-list, a command palette, step-switch hotkeys, monospace IDs, streaming tokens into a watch list. This is precisely the productivity-tool template (dashboard, density, keyboard-driven) the product defines itself against. Its own tradeoffs section admits divergence from voyage calm and calls it intentional, conceding it breaks the DNA. The target user is a non-developer strategist; command-palette cockpits serve power-developers, not the persona, and the calm-judgment moat versus just-ask-ChatGPT is lost the moment the screen becomes a control panel. Fidelity 1. Value 2 because returning-user fast navigation is a legitimate need met the wrong way. Feasibility 3: large but tractable, and it gates itself behind a settings opt-in reusing existing step components. Salvage only the assumption-status dots and the traceability tags; reject the cockpit frame wholesale.

recommendation.surface: Core voyage flow — interaction model & information architecture
recommendation.recommended_direction: Adopt "Focused-Linear" (Calming Full-Screen Canvas) as the base interaction model, but deliver it as an INCREMENTAL re-skin of the existing ProgressiveFlow shell — not a from-scratch rewrite. The voyage becomes four ceremonially-separated "legs," each a calm centered canvas (max-w-2xl, one question at center, per §3.1), bracketed by step-exit "AnchoringMoment" cards and step-entry "context carry-forward" narration (per §3.2). The invisible context-accumulation chain (the §2.2 moat) is made visible in THREE complementary, low-cost ways grafted from the runners-up: (1) inline provenance tags ("← 항로 재설정 Q2에서") on every carried-forward field, grafted from Command Deck; (2) a toggleable gold dashed ancestry thread inside the EXISTING declarative BranchMap, grafted from Atlas — NOT a new imperative pan/zoom renderer; (3) assumption verification promoted to a first-class ✓/미검증 toggle in the existing Logbook rail's per-checkpoint assumption drill-down, grafted from Atlas but rendered as a plain list, not spatial diamonds. Refinement convergence gets Atlas's compass-rose glyph (driven by the existing convergence_score) in the Step-4 header and its AnchoringMoment. The existing Logbook rail is RE-FRAMED as the persistent "VoyageGuide": original problem + current leg purpose + collapsed prior-leg summaries on top, the live ship's-log waypoints below. Outputs stage into a "이타카 (Delivery Hall)" full-page panel after the refine loop, built on the EXISTING lib/export.ts markdown (Voyage-Log headline trail), with a deferred html2canvas-based PNG as a strictly later enhancement. The dense Command Deck cockpit and the Atlas-as-default 3-column atlas are REJECTED as defaults (they violate §3 calm + §6 anti-dashboard DNA); their power-user value is preserved only as an optional, hidden keyboard layer (Express Mode / Cmd-jump) gated behind a layoutPreference, never in the first-run UI.
recommendation.rationale: All three judge lenses converged on Focused-Linear as the truest extension of the voyage DNA: it makes §3.1 (calm near-empty screen, one question at center) and §3.2 (transition messages that narrate context carry-forward) literal, and its AnchoringMoment ritual IS the §6.2 ship's-bell / §10 "breath between legs." It also most directly beats the real competitor ("just ask ChatGPT") for a non-developer strategist by lowering cognitive load and making the AI's context-carry visibly trustworthy — the single thing ChatGPT cannot show. The two runners-up were each penalized hard where they matter: Atlas's imperative voyage-chart-renderer FIGHTS the codebase (BranchMap is already declarative; branch_id is deliberately NOT stored — lineage is computed via getActivePath; classified_risks/hidden_assumptions are nested in state_snapshot, not flat per-checkpoint; html2canvas is uninstalled and can't cleanly rasterize var(--…) SVG fills), and a 3-column legend/chart/manifest is the AI-dashboard density §6 explicitly bans. Command Deck self-admittedly diverges from voyage calm into a cmd+k cockpit built for developers, the exact wrong persona. BUT every judge independently flagged the same grafts as the highest-value, lowest-cost wins — ancestry thread, provenance tags, first-class assumption verification, the convergence compass — and noted they can ALL land on existing primitives (BranchMap, Logbook, convergence_score, lib/export.ts) WITHOUT the dangerous full refactor or any new dependency. The decisive correction from the design-engineer and philosophy judges: do NOT rewrite the 2670-line ProgressiveFlow (it inlines worker deployment, forking, verification gates, streaming; rewriting regresses lateral-jump + inline-output and breaks flow-interactions/logbook tests). Instead re-skin its existing centered column into per-leg canvases with additive AnchoringMoment/VoyageGuide/ContextCarryToast components, preserving the 1004-test baseline. The philosophy judge's color correction is honored: the focused-linear spec's proposed cold-blue (#2d4a7c) and purple (#6b4c9a) step accents violate §6's explicit ban — remapped to the warm navy/charcoal + gold/amber family, reserving risk-purple (#7F77DD) for rehearse risk context only.
recommendation.concrete_spec:
GOAL: Four calm legs, ceremonial transitions, visible context chain — built ON existing primitives, no new deps in the default path.

═══ A. SHELL & LEG CANVAS (re-skin, not rewrite) ═══
Keep src/app/workspace/page.tsx's flex shell (flex-1 centered column + sticky right rail). Do NOT restructure ProgressiveFlow.tsx wholesale. Instead introduce a thin presentational frame that ProgressiveFlow's existing phase blocks render INTO.

New: src/components/workspace/progressive/shared/LegCanvas.tsx
  Props: { leg: 1|2|3|4; legKey: 'reframe'|'recast'|'rehearse'|'refine'; busy: boolean; children; onAdvance?: ()=>void; advanceDisabled?: boolean; anchoringSummary?: AnchoringSummary }
  Layout: <section className="max-w-2xl mx-auto px-4 md:px-6 py-8">
    - Leg header (one row): "{leg} / 4 · {legKo} · {legEn}" + lucide icon. Serif, text-[var(--text-primary)]. e.g. "1 / 4 · 항로 재설정 · Reframe".
    - One centering question line under header (text-[15px] serif text-[var(--text-secondary)]): the §3.x microcopy, e.g. "이 과제가 정말로 묻고 있는 것은 무엇입니까?".
    - {children}: the EXISTING analysis/question/worker cards, unchanged.
    - Footer advance row (only on a settled leg): [← 이전] ghost + [다음 → {nextLegKo}] primary (disabled until advanceDisabled===false).
  Entry motion: framer-motion initial {opacity:0,y:-16} animate {opacity:1,y:0}, transition EASE = cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) ~0.5s (token already exists). Exit {opacity:0,y:16}.
  Leg accent map (§6-compliant — NO cold blue / no purple chrome):
    reframe  → var(--text-primary) deep navy/charcoal; icon MessageSquare
    recast   → var(--accent) gold/amber;               icon Sliders  (this is the §10 moment-2 "전체가 보인다" leg — give it the warmest accent)
    rehearse → var(--text-secondary) muted navy;        icon UserCheck (risk-purple #7F77DD used ONLY inside risk chips, never as chrome)
    refine   → var(--accent) gold/amber;                icon RefreshCw
  ProgressiveFlow maps its phase→leg: reframe = phase∈{input,conversing(round<2),analyzing(round1)}; recast = mixing/lead_synthesizing/conversing-with-mix; rehearse = dm_feedback; refine = refining; complete → Delivery Hall. Reuse the existing phaseIdx() logic (page.tsx:132) as the source of truth — do not invent a parallel state machine.

═══ B. ANCHORING MOMENT (step-exit ritual, §3.2/§6.2/§10) ═══
New: src/components/workspace/progressive/shared/AnchoringMoment.tsx
  Modal (reuse ui/Modal). Centered card: bg-[var(--surface)], rounded-2xl, border-l-4 border-[var(--accent)], shadow-[var(--shadow-lg)], max-w-md, text-center, generous py-8.
  Content = the EXACT §3.2 transition copy keyed by leg→leg:
    reframe→recast:  "항로가 잡혔습니다. 이제 각자의 자리를 배정합니다." + 1-line summary "진짜 질문: {real_question} · 숨은 전제 {n}개"
    recast→rehearse: "선원이 배치되었습니다. 출항 전 한 번 항로를 쳐봅니다." + "핵심 방향: {governing_idea} · 배치 {n}단계"
    rehearse→refine: "첫 선원 회의가 끝났습니다. 피드백을 반영해 항로를 다시 잡습니다." + "식별된 리스크: 🔴{c}/🟡{m}/🟣{u}"
    refine→ithaca:   "항로가 잡혔습니다. 이타카로 향할 준비가 되었습니다." + ConvergenceRose at {convergence_score}%
  Single CTA: "{nextLegKo}로" (e.g. "선원 배치로"). Back-navigation never triggers this ritual (calm forward only; reversal is fast).
  Wires into existing phase-advance handlers in ProgressiveFlow (the points that today call into recast/rehearse/refine) — gate the actual phase transition behind the modal's CTA.

═══ C. VOYAGEGUIDE = re-framed Logbook rail (§3.2 chain visible) ═══
Modify src/components/workspace/progressive/Logbook.tsx (additive top section; keep waypoint <ol> below untouched):
  Add a top block ABOVE the branch switcher:
    1. "이 항해" — original problem (read-only, line-clamp-3, text-[12px]).
    2. "현재 항계 · {legKo}" + the leg's guiding question (the same one shown in LegCanvas header).
    3. "지나온 항로" — collapsed prior-leg summary cards (one per completed leg), each showing the leg's key decision (reframe→real_question; recast→governing_idea; rehearse→risk counts). Click to expand the snapshot; this reuses the existing assumptionsByCp drill-down pattern.
  Provenance tags (graft from Command Deck): each carried-forward summary card renders an inline origin label, e.g. "← 항로 재설정에서" / "← 가정 #3 미검증", text-[10px] text-[var(--text-tertiary)]. Source from the typed ContextChain._source metadata (ROADMAP Phase 0) when available; fall back to leg name.

═══ D. ASSUMPTION VERIFICATION as first-class object (graft Atlas, render as list) ═══
The data already exists: state_snapshot.snapshots[-1].hidden_assumptions (Logbook already reads it via assumptionsByCp, line 68-70).
  Store: add to useProgressiveStore a method
    markAssumptionVerified(checkpointId: string, index: number, verified: boolean)
    → updates session.checkpoints[].state_snapshot.snapshots[-1] with a parallel verified-flags array (new optional field assumption_verified?: boolean[] on the snapshot type — schema-sync Supabase per CLAUDE.md checklist). Defensive access: (snapshot.assumption_verified || []).
  UI: in Logbook's existing "이 시점의 가정 {n}" <details> drill-down (line 247-261), render each assumption with a leading toggle:
    [✓] verified → text-[var(--success)], strikethrough; [○] unverified → text-[var(--accent)] dot.
    Toggle calls markAssumptionVerified. This directly drives ROADMAP success metric "평균 전제 확인됨 마킹 수 > 0.5개/세션" and manufactures §10 moment #1.

═══ E. ANCESTRY THREAD overlay (graft Atlas, into EXISTING declarative BranchMap) ═══
Modify src/components/workspace/progressive/BranchMap.tsx — add ONE optional prop and ONE layer, no imperative renderer, no pan/zoom, no new dep:
  New prop: showAncestry?: boolean (default false).
  When true, draw a thin gold dashed <path> from the current leg's node back to its prior-stage source node, reusing the existing edgePath() S-curve helper:
    <path d={edgePath(prior.x,prior.y,cur.x,cur.y)} fill="none" stroke="var(--accent)" strokeWidth="1" strokeDasharray="4 2" opacity="0.7" />
  prior/current resolved from getActivePath lineage (already imported pattern) — NOT from a stored branch_id (which deliberately doesn't exist). Toggle lives as a single "맥락 체인 보기" checkbox in the VoyageChart modal header (Logbook line 283 already mounts <VoyageChart/> in a Modal). This is the highest-fidelity "moat made visible" move at ~15 lines.

═══ F. CONVERGENCE COMPASS (graft Atlas glyph) ═══
New: src/components/workspace/progressive/shared/ConvergenceRose.tsx
  Small SVG compass rose; needle rotates rotate(${score*3.6}deg) toward True North. Driven by existing convergence_score (types.ts:709) / assessConvergence() (progressive-convergence.ts:29). Warm gold needle on cream. Tooltip "수렴도: {score}%".
  Placement: Step-4 (refine) LegCanvas header (replacing any generic progress bar) AND the refine→ithaca AnchoringMoment. Pairs with the §2.5 copy: "항로 지수: {score}% — 한 번 더 항로를 잡아보시겠습니까?".

═══ G. 이타카 / DELIVERY HALL (defer outputs; build on existing export) ═══
On phase==='complete', render a full-width "이타카" panel (reuse the centered column; collapse the rail) with 4 tabs (항해일지/선원 지시서/전체 해도/점검표) rendered via the EXISTING lib/export.ts + agent-spec.ts + checklist.ts markdown — NO change to those generators required.
  Headline of 항해일지 (Project Brief) = a Voyage-Log trail built from the existing waypoints (⚓ 출항 → ↻ 침로 변경 → ⚠ 암초 → ⚑ 정박) — the WP_META glyph set already exists in Logbook (line 32-40); reuse it.
  Actions: 복사 / .md 다운로드 (existing) + "항해로 돌아가기" (returns to refine for more looping — preserves the lateral access focused-linear otherwise regresses).
  DEFERRED (separate ticket, NOT in default path): "해도 다운로드" PNG via html2canvas — only added behind a flag, with a native SVG-serialize→canvas fallback because html2canvas can't reliably rasterize var(--…) custom-property fills. Honors §1.3 "해도 자체가 지식" without blocking the calm core.

═══ H. POWER LAYER (graft Command Deck, hidden) ═══
useWorkspaceStore: add layoutPreference: 'calm' (default) — calm IS the only first-run path. Optional, off-by-default, settings-gated keyboard affordances: Back/Next on arrow keys, "Express Mode" (skip to recast when a reframe already exists), Cmd+2/3/4 leg-jump. NO command palette, NO cmd+k, NO dense cockpit in default UI. This satisfies returning users without imposing density on first-time strategists.
grafted_from_runners_up: From Atlas: toggleable gold dashed ANCESTRY THREAD rendered inside the EXISTING declarative BranchMap (reusing edgePath + getActivePath lineage), NOT a new imperative pan/zoom voyage-chart-renderer — the single highest-fidelity 'context-chain made visible' move at ~15 lines, zero new deps.

From Atlas: assumption VERIFICATION as a first-class ✓/미검증 toggle, surfaced in the Logbook's existing per-checkpoint assumption drill-down as a plain list (NOT spatial diamonds), driving ROADMAP metric '전제 확인됨 마킹 > 0.5/세션' and §10 moment #1.

From Atlas: the CONVERGENCE COMPASS-ROSE glyph driven by the existing convergence_score / assessConvergence(), placed in the refine leg header + its AnchoringMoment — a calm single-glyph replacement for a generic progress bar.

From Atlas: the chart-as-shareable-ARTIFACT idea (§1.3 해도 자체가 지식) realized FIRST as the Voyage-Log markdown headline in the existing Project Brief export, with the html2canvas PNG explicitly deferred behind a flag (uninstalled dep + can't rasterize var(--…) fills).

From Command Deck: inline context-ORIGIN/PROVENANCE tags ('← 항로 재설정 Q2에서', '← 가정 #3 미검증') on every carried-forward field, sourced from typed ContextChain._source — grafted into the VoyageGuide summary cards and ContextCarryToast, the cheapest highest-trust proof the AI carried thinking forward.

From Command Deck: a strictly-optional, hidden keyboard/power layer (Back/Next keys, Express Mode skip-to-recast, Cmd-jump) gated behind layoutPreference='calm' default — returning-user speed WITHOUT cmd+k cockpit density or DNA violation.
acceptance_criteria: First-run user sees ONE leg at a time: a centered max-w-2xl canvas with a single guiding question at center, no competing panels above the fold (§3.1). The 1004-test baseline still passes (flow-interactions, logbook-render, voyagechart-render unaffected because ProgressiveFlow is re-skinned, not rewritten).

Every forward leg transition shows an AnchoringMoment modal with the exact §3.2 transition copy + a 1-line carry-forward summary, and the actual phase transition only fires on its CTA. Backward navigation does NOT trigger the ritual.

The VoyageGuide (re-framed Logbook rail) always shows: original problem (read-only), current leg + guiding question, and collapsed prior-leg summary cards — each summary carries an inline provenance tag ('← {legKo}에서').

Toggling '맥락 체인 보기' in the Full-Chart modal draws a gold dashed ancestry thread from the current leg's node to its prior-stage source node in BranchMap, using the existing edgePath helper and getActivePath lineage (no stored branch_id, no new component).

Each hidden assumption in the Logbook drill-down has a working ✓/미검증 toggle; toggling persists via markAssumptionVerified (with Supabase column synced per CLAUDE.md) and survives reload via defensive access. Marking ≥1 assumption is reachable in ≤2 clicks from any settled leg.

The refine leg header and its AnchoringMoment render a ConvergenceRose whose needle angle = convergence_score*3.6°, sourced from assessConvergence() — no separate generic progress bar remains on that leg.

On completion, an 이타카 Delivery Hall presents all 4 outputs via the existing export generators unchanged, with the 항해일지 leading on a ⚓→↻→⚠→⚑ Voyage-Log trail built from existing waypoints + WP_META glyphs; '항해로 돌아가기' returns to refine.

No new runtime dependency is added to the default path (html2canvas/cmdk absent); the PNG export and any command palette exist only behind explicit, off-by-default flags. All leg-chrome accents are warm navy/charcoal/gold — no cold #2d4a7c blue or #6b4c9a purple chrome; risk-purple #7F77DD appears only inside rehearse risk chips (§6).
recommendation.sequencing_note: Depends on TWO foundation items and is explicitly scoped to AVOID a third. (1) ROADMAP Phase 0 typed pipeline / ContextChain._source metadata is the clean source for the provenance tags (Section C/H) — until it lands, fall back to leg-name labels, so this work is not blocked but improves when Phase 0 ships. (2) The CLAUDE.md add-a-field checklist applies to the new snapshot.assumption_verified[] field (Section D): type def + store creator + DEFAULT + Supabase migration + any prompt that reads it. (3) Critically, this direction is deliberately decoupled from a full ProgressiveFlow decomposition: it re-skins the existing 2670-line component via additive LegCanvas/AnchoringMoment/VoyageGuide/ConvergenceRose presentational components and reuses the existing phaseIdx() state logic, so it does NOT wait on (and does not trigger) the risky carousel rewrite that would regress lateral-jump, inline outputs, and the test suite. Suggested build order: B (AnchoringMoment) + C (VoyageGuide rail) first — pure-additive, ship calm-ceremony value immediately on today's flow; then A (LegCanvas re-skin) once those are proven; then D/E/F (verification toggle, ancestry thread, compass) as independent grafts; then G (Delivery Hall) last; H (power layer) and the PNG artifact are post-MVP flags.

designed.title: Output artifacts (이타카) — Brief / Prompt Chain / Agent Spec / Checklist

concepts.angle: Executable Artifacts — Contextual, Stateful, Checkpointiable Outputs
concepts.concept_name: Live Execution Suite: Prompt Chain as Interactive Runbook, Agent Spec with Assumption Validation, Checklist with Real-time State
concepts.the_idea: Transform four static markdown outputs into a unified, interconnected execution system where Prompt Chain runs step-by-step with baked-in voyage context (showing which assumption each prompt validates, what happens if it fails); Agent Spec embeds abort conditions and feeds-into dependencies; and Checklist becomes a live Supabase-persisted interactive document with real-time assumption verification feedback. The artifacts don't just describe the voyage—they *guide* it.
key_moves: Prompt Chain → Interactive Runbook UI: Each prompt card displays its source (which reframe assumption justified it), assumption it validates, success checkpoints before next prompt, abort/pivot conditions. Copy/run with one click, but the full context stays visible.

Agent Spec → Executable DAG: Embed `validates_assumption` + `abort_condition` + `feeds_into` fields directly in YAML; UI renders as a live dependency graph where assumption verification cascades into step warnings/greyouts.

Checklist → Supabase-Backed Live Document: Checkbox state persists; when assumptions are verified elsewhere (in live prompt execution), checklist auto-updates. Breakpoints show 'waiting for assumption X' state.

Contextual Handoff: Each artifact card shows a mini-breadcrumb of voyage decisions (from which reframe frame, which key assumption justified this, what persona concern does this address). Provenance as metadata, not footnotes.

Abort/Pivot UI: When a prompt execution reveals an assumption is false, a modal offers: (a) pivot to contingency prompt (pre-drafted), (b) return to recast & modify, (c) update assumption→cascade to downstream. Not a dead-end, a fork.
Run-in-Place Toggle: Quick toggle between 'read static markdown' (copy-paste mode) and 'interactive execution' (with Claude API hooks or form-field capture for each prompt's result).

## Design Decisions: Why This Matters

1. **Prompt Chain as Runbook, Not Copyable Block**
   - Current: User reads markdown, copy-pastes into Claude manually
   - New: Each step is a card with validation checkpoint built in. User can "Run in Claude" (API call) or paste result (form). System automatically validates assumption, updates downstream steps. **The artifact becomes a living guide, not a frozen plan.**

2. **Abort Conditions as First-Class Citizens**
   - Current: Assumptions are suggested, but no hard stop if wrong
   - New: When executing, if a prompt result reveals assumption false, execution pauses. User has 3 options: pivot to contingency, back up & modify plan, skip to alt branch. **The harness does what it's for: prevents sailing off the edge.**

3. **Assumption Graph as UI, Not Metadata**
   - Current: Agent Spec lists assumptions in YAML, no visual linkage to steps
   - New: DAG visualization shows which steps validate which assumptions, what happens downstream if one fails. Clicking assumption shows all steps affected. **Visualizing the dependency web is the core insight that makes the whole thing executable.**

4. **Checklist as Supabase Mirror, Not Local Markdown**
   - Current: Checklist is markdown, user checks off locally, never synced
   - New: Each checkbox state stored in Supabase; assumption verification auto-cascades (if assumption X verified in execution, all checklist items "validate assumption X" auto-check). **Execution log becomes the source of truth for downstream states.**

5. **Contextual Breadcrumbs Over Footnotes**
   - Current: "This step validates assumption_2" is in a comment somewhere
   - New: Every artifact card shows its lineage: "Reframe 'Q1' → Recast Step 3 → Persona CFO concern 'ROI'" in a small trail above the main content. **The user never forgets why this step exists.**

6. **Interactive Mode is Opt-In, Not Default**
   - Current: All artifacts are read-only markdown
   - New: Toggle switch "Read" ↔ "Interactive". Read mode = same as today (copy-paste friendly). Interactive = form inputs, Claude API integration, real-time assumption feedback. **Non-builders can use it as-is; power users have a full execution environment.**

---

## Buildability Checklist

- ✓ Leverages existing stores (useProjectStore, useProgressiveStore, useWorkspaceStore)
- ✓ Reuses existing export functions as data source; extends with structure
- ✓ No breaking changes to current phase flow (adds new step after Refinement)
- ✓ Supabase migrations are optional (falls back to localStorage for MVP)
- ✓ Design tokens already support all needed colors (risk colors, actor colors, checkpoint highlight)
- ✓ Interactive mode can start MVP-simple: form inputs only, no API calls
- ✓ Tests can validate: assumption graph building, checklist auto-update logic, DAG rendering

concepts.tradeoffs:
**Tradeoffs Accepted:**

1. **Complexity for Users Who Just Want Markdown**
   - Arg: Runbook UI + interactive mode adds cognitive load for copy-paste users.
   - Mitigation: "Read" mode is default, visually identical to current markdown. Interactive mode is a toggle; non-power-users never see it.
   - Bet: Benefit of guided execution (assumption validation, abort conditions, auto-cascading state) > cost of extra UI option.

2. **More LLM Calls (if auto-execution enabled)**
   - Arg: Every prompt execution could call Claude API for validation.
   - Mitigation: "Run in Claude" is optional; user can paste result manually. Validation is heuristic-based (simple regex checks on success checkpoints), not a Claude call.
   - Bet: MVP launches with manual form input; auto-execution is post-launch feature.

3. **Supabase Dependency for Live State**
   - Arg: Checklist state needs sync; localStorage alone insufficient for multi-device use.
   - Mitigation: Graceful degradation: localStorage-first, async Supabase sync. Offline still works, syncs when reconnected.
   - Bet: Users expect artifacts to persist across sessions; Supabase is a cost worth paying.

4. **Assumption Graph as DAG Adds ~400 lines Code**
   - Arg: LiveAgentSpec DAG component + assumption-linking logic increases codebase size.
   - Mitigation: Component is isolated (in outputs/ folder), doesn't touch core voyage flow. Easy to disable or stub if needed.
   - Bet: Assumption graph is the core insight that makes "executable" mean something; worth the size.

5. **"Abort Condition" Requires Explicit User Action**
   - Arg: Can't auto-detect assumption failure; user must either confirm or pivot manually.
   - Mitigation: By design — the goal is to *surface* the failure so the user can judge, not to automate away their judgment. This honors the harness philosophy ("hear but don't leap").
   - Bet: A hard stop with choices is better than silent cascading failure.

**What This Gives Up (& Why):**
- No full agent framework integration (LangGraph/CrewAI integration is post-launch)
- No multi-user real-time collaboration on artifacts (designed for individual execution, team review is separate)
- No AI-driven assumption auto-validation (heuristic only in MVP)
- No automatic pivot suggestion (user chooses from pre-drafted contingencies)

**Where This Shines:**
- Transforms artifacts from "read-once copy-paste" to "living execution guides"
- Closes the loop: every decision made in voyage flow (reframe frame, key assumption, persona concern) is visible and actionable in execution
- Makes "abort condition" and "assumption validation" first-class mechanics, not buried in persona feedback
- Validates the core Argus thesis: *the process itself (deciding, validating, pivoting) is the deliverable*, not just the final plan

Each line of the final artifacts visibly traces back to the voyage moment that produced it—from hidden assumption through reframing decision, rehearsal insight, or refinement feedback. This turns "copy-paste payoff" into "decision record proven by its own provenance."
key_moves: Provenance tracking: Every output field carries a `_source` metadata chain (phase → itemId → field → userModified flag) that users can hover/click to see the 'why' of that line

Narrative framing in Brief: Reorder from static sections into a ship's-log structure—출발 가설 (departure hypothesis) → 암초 발견 (reefs encountered) → 침로 수정 (course corrections) → 이타카 (Ithaca reached)—so the Brief is the voyage story, not a generic plan

Agent Spec as decision forest: Instead of flat YAML, render the workflow as a dependency graph where assumption nodes link to validating steps, and risks (from rehearsal) link to affected workflow branches with abort conditions

Checklist as decision journal: Checkpoints don't just mark task completion; they're tied to assumption validation results—checking a box updates downstream assumption certainty, which propagates to related checkpoints

Expandable attribution sidebar: A persistent right-rail (or drawer) showing the full provenance chain for any selected output section; click 'Why?' and see the decompose answer, recast reasoning, rehearsal concern, and refinement that shaped it
concepts.tradeoffs:
## What This Gains vs. Current State

**Gains:**
1. **Decision transparency** — Every line of output can be traced to the moment it was decided. Users (and their stakeholders) see "this assumption came from reframing" or "this checkpoint was added because CFO raised ROI risk in rehearsal." No orphaned statements.

2. **Narrative coherence** — Brief tells the voyage story (departure → obstacles → course-corrections → destination) rather than listing generic deliverables. The user sees the *why* of the plan, not just the *what*.

3. **Live propagation** — When an assumption is marked verified, downstream outputs update automatically (checkpoint removed, related risks downgrade, assumption certainty increases). No copy-paste mismatch.

4. **Power-user depth + novice clarity** — Casual users see clean documents. Power users click "Why?" and explore the full provenance chain without cluttering the main view.

5. **Execution confidence** — AI/human executor reads a prompt and instantly knows: (a) what assumption it's validating, (b) what risks it mitigates, (c) what govern ing idea it serves. No ambiguity about "why am I doing this step?"

---

## What This Costs / Trade-offs

1. **Engineering effort** — New provenance metadata system, new component tier (Brief 2.0, Prompt Cards, etc.), Supabase schema updates. Estimated Phase 5 work: 1.5–2 weeks vs. 1–1.5 weeks for naive "just pretty-print markdown" approach.

2. **UX complexity for simple users** — The source-link system (hoverable anchors, sidebar) adds visual real estate and cognitive load for users who just want a clean export. *Mitigation:* provenance is opt-in (checkbox in FinalCard), default export is clean.

3. **Storage overhead** — Storing `ProvenanceNode[]` for every output field means ~1.5–2× more data in Supabase. For most projects this is negligible, but at scale (10k+ users, years of data) is notable. *Mitigation:* compress provenance chains; prune after 6 months; defer archival.

4. **Assumption dependency graph complexity** — Building the full DAG of assumptions + steps + risks is computationally harder than flat lists. With 20+ assumptions and 15 steps, rendering an interactive graph gets laggy. *Mitigation:* lazy-load graph (show top 5 critical nodes, rest behind "expand"), memoize with React.useMemo.

5. **Export fragility** — When exporting to external tools (LangGraph YAML, email, Notion), the HTML-based provenance links break. *Mitigation:* offer YAML export with provenance as inline comments, plain-text export with footnotes (# [^1] references), and HTML export (self-contained with inline styles).

6. **Pedagogical burden** — The feature assumes users want to learn *why* they made decisions. Some users prefer speed over reflection. *Mitigation:* provenance is never mandatory; even without it, output is usable.

---

## Why This Angle (Narrative-Provenance) Over Alternatives

**vs. "Execution-Ready" (live checklist, abort conditions, real-time status):**
- Provenance focuses on *understanding decisions made*; execution-ready focuses on *monitoring decisions in flight*. This is complementary, not competing—provenance can be a prereq for later execution-ready features. Provenance is the "before", execution-ready is the "during."

**vs. "Knowledge Synthesis" (cross-project pattern learning, collective intelligence):**
- Provenance is *single-journey introspection*; synthesis is *multi-journey aggregation*. Provenance enables synthesis (by providing clean, structured metadata), but synthesis is a downstream benefit. Provenance is the foundation.

**vs. "Collaborative Refinement" (team reviews, async feedback loops, final-draft versioning):**
- Provenance is about tracing *why a line exists*, not *who wrote it or what they debated*. Provenance can feed into team review, but team review is an orchestration layer above provenance.

**Why narrative-provenance is the *right* angle:** Argus's core thesis is "think before you recast"—the voyage itself (출발 → 암초 → 침로 수정 → 이타카) is the point, not just the final output. Narrative-provenance honors this by making the outputs *tell the story of the voyage*, not erase it. Every line of the Brief, Prompt Chain, Spec, and Checklist becomes a memory of a decision moment. This is what "the process is the deliverable" actually looks like in artifacts.

---

## Edge Cases & Future Openness

1. **Assumption marked unverified mid-flight:** If user decides "actually, we never validated this" after execution started, provenance system marks it as "assumption_reversed" and surfaces all downstream outputs that depend on it. UX shows a warning card.

2. **Branching voyages (already in Argus):** Each branch has its own provenance chain. When merging branches, show provenance conflict resolution UI.

3. **Handoff to external teams:** When exporting Agent Spec to LangGraph/CrewAI team, provenance comments in YAML act as embedded documentation. External team doesn't see the interactive UI but gets the "why" as structured metadata.

4. **Multi-phase projects:** If a project spans weeks with new decompose → recast → rehearsal cycles, provenance builds a *longitudinal history* (not just current state). Useful for learning "what changed from v1.0 to v2.0 and why."

5. **Assumption-centric dashboard (future):** Once provenance data is rich, build a separate view showing "all assumptions across all projects" with validation status, risk heatmap, critical-path highlighting. This becomes Phase 6 (Cross-User Intelligence) fodder.

concepts.tradeoffs:
**Complexity vs. Usability**: Adding downstream tool detection + multiple output variants increases component logic significantly (ChecklistLive, HandoffIntegrityModal, destination selector). Mitigated by: (1) lazy-load variants only when user engages tool selector, (2) sensible defaults (detect intent from recent actions), (3) one-click send that hides format complexity.

**Supabase Dependency for Checklist**: Making checklist "live" with real-time sync requires Supabase schema additions (checklist_items table) and connection stability. If offline, falls back to localStorage + eventual sync. Trade-off accepted because assumption validation failures must propagate instantly to prevent downstream errors; eventual consistency is dangerous for safety gates.

**Prompt Chain Verbosity**: Adding inline provenance + abort conditions + decision markers substantially expands prompt text (1.5x–2x length). Some users may find it noisy. Mitigated by: (1) toggle between "clean" (human-friendly) and "annotated" (tool-ready) versions, (2) annotations are always in comments/code blocks, (3) Claude/ChatGPT can ignore metadata if context length is tight.

**Handoff Integrity Modal Friction**: Requiring user to confirm handoff contents before copying adds one modal before every send. Risk: users skip reading and become desensitized to warnings. Mitigated by: (1) modal is brief (3-4 bullet points max), (2) highlights ONLY critical deltas ("3 abort conditions", "2 human gates") not every detail, (3) defaults to "copy anyway" button but requires deliberate dismissal, not just clicking through.

**Offline / No-Supabase Fallback**: If user doesn't have Supabase auth, ChecklistLive degrades to localStorage-only + manual sync button. This is acceptable for MVP; real-time sync is a Phase 5 stretch goal, not blocking launch.

**Tool Coverage**: Designed for 6 tools (Claude API, Claude Web, ChatGPT, CrewAI, LangGraph, Cursor). Other tools (Anthropic Bedrock, LangChain, n8n) not included in this pass. Future: extensible registry pattern allows easy addition without refactoring.

**Assumption Linking Complexity**: Mapping assumptions from decompose → recast steps → agent-spec validation steps requires careful ID tracking across multiple LLM generations. If assumptions drift linguistically (same idea, different wording), the linker may fail to recognize them. Mitigated by: (1) explicit assumption IDs in decompose output (a1, a2, a3...), (2) recast output explicitly references assumption IDs, (3) visual review in Handoff Integrity Modal before send.

**Privacy / Sharing Concern**: Voyage log + decision trail embedded in exported artifacts means sensitive reasoning becomes visible to whoever receives the document (e.g., external stakeholders). Mitigated by: (1) option to export "clean" version without voyage log, (2) toggle in final card already exists (current feature), (3) Handoff Integrity Modal warns "This includes your decision trail" for extended versions.

**Convergence with Existing UX**: Phase 5 explicitly targets "artifacts as first-class handoffs" — this concept directly implements that goal. Risk: existing users expect static markdown exports; adding tool-aware variants may confuse. Mitigated by: (1) defaults to familiar markdown export, (2) tool selector is opt-in (second panel), (3) existing "Copy" button unchanged, new "Send to [Tool]" buttons appear below it.

recommendation.recommended_direction:
Attributable Ithaca — turn the four outputs into a single ship's-log decision record where every line traces back to the voyage moment that produced it, and where the Agent Spec is the one and only sanctioned bridge down into execution tooling.

Base: concept #2 "Attributable Outputs: Narrative + Provenance" (unanimous judge winner: best target-user value, highest philosophy fidelity, most buildable because the plumbing already ships). The spine is a four-act ship's-log Brief (출항 departure hypothesis → 암초 reefs → 침로 수정 course-correction → 이타카 Ithaca) and a "Why?" provenance anchor on every output line that opens a warm editorial annotation tracing decompose→recast→rehearse→refine.

Grafted from runners-up (judge-flagged): (a) per-prompt provenance footnote in Prompt Chain citing originating reframe assumption + rehearsal risk; (b) abort/contingency as a *readable fork note inside the artifact*, NOT a live execution modal — static text only; (c) per-tool variant generation (CrewAI YAML + LangGraph JSON) confined to the Agent Spec ONLY, since that is the designated handoff to the execution layer; (d) clean-vs-handoff export toggle, an evolution of the existing FinalCard 항해일지 checkbox; (e) a one-line handoff-integrity summary before copy/share ("이 묶음에는 미확인 전제 3건, 사람 판단 2건이 들어있습니다").

Explicitly REJECTED (all three judges penalized): live execution console, Run-in-Claude buttons, useExecutionStore runtime, Supabase execution_logs/checklist_states tables, status pills, cold node-graph DAGs, six-tool intent sniffing, blue=AI/green=human dashboard coloring. Argus is the judgment layer ABOVE execution (Philosophy §7); Ithaca is a quiet landfall, not mission control.

The single most important foundation fix folded in: replace the fragile substring assumption-linker (`step.task.includes(a.assumption.substring(0,8))` in agent-spec.ts:104 and prompt-chain.ts:150-153) with explicit stable assumption IDs flowing through the typed context chain. Provenance is only trustworthy if the links are real.
recommendation.rationale:
Why this base wins for THIS surface and THIS user. The target user is a non-developer strategist whose real competitor is "just asking ChatGPT directly." Against that rival, a static markdown plan is barely differentiated — ChatGPT also emits markdown. What ChatGPT cannot produce is an artifact that *shows its own reasoning genealogy*: "this success metric became 18-month NPV because the CFO persona raised an ROI reef in rehearsal." That is Philosophy §10 Moment 5 (the process was more valuable than the output) made literal and §3.3 (the output moment where the user sees the charted hypothesis realized). All three judges ranked this #1 on philosophy fidelity; two ranked it #1 overall; the craft judge gave it 5/5 feasibility because the outputs are pure string generators and the provenance plumbing already exists (context-chain.ts typed contexts, voyageLogToMarkdown, FinalCard opt-in toggle, AttributedSection data-attribution-source hooks, agent-spec already emits validates_assumption + warnings, prompt-chain already injects risk_if_false).

Why the two runners-up lose as a base but win as grafts. Live Execution Suite (#1 in JSON) scored 2/2/2-3 across the board: it builds a runtime console for a developer-operator who is not the user, drags Argus into the LangGraph/CrewAI layer it refuses to be, and makes the fragile substring linker safety-critical. Executable Ithaca over-rotates on dev tooling (cursor rules, curl snippets, six-tool selector) and a Supabase live checklist with ABORT badges — generic-dashboard texture §6 bans. But each carries exactly one transplantable organ: the Live Suite's "abort as a fork not a dead-end" idea (rendered as static contingency text, honoring "hear but don't leap"), and Ithaca's per-tool Agent-Spec variants + integrity summary. The judges independently converged on these same grafts.

Why provenance must come with the linker fix. The whole value proposition is "every line traces to a real decision." If the trace is built on `task.includes(substring(0,8))` it will silently mislink or drop links, and a wrong provenance arrow is worse than none — it lies to the strategist about why a step exists. So the linker upgrade is not optional polish; it is load-bearing for the headline feature.

Why this stays faithful to the dawn-harbor mood. The risk the philosophy judge flagged is that a provenance/assumption graph drifts cold and DAG-like. The spec below renders provenance as warm serif marginalia (gold dotted underlines, a slow-spring annotation panel in ivory), never as a node graph in the strategist-facing surfaces. The only graph-shaped output (LangGraph JSON) lives behind the Agent Spec's developer-handoff tab where a dev, not the strategist, consumes it.
recommendation.concrete_spec:
## Architecture overview
Keep the four generators as pure string functions (no new runtime, no stores, no Supabase tables). Refactor them to consume a shared typed `IthacaContext` and emit, alongside their markdown, a parallel `AttributedField[]` array carrying provenance. Render strategist-facing surfaces from `AttributedField[]`; keep markdown as the copy/export payload.

### 0. FOUNDATION FIX (prerequisite, do first): stable assumption IDs
Files: `src/stores/types.ts`, `src/lib/context-chain.ts`, `src/lib/agent-spec.ts`, `src/lib/prompt-chain.ts`.
- `HiddenAssumption` gains `id?: string` (stable, e.g. `a1`,`a2`… assigned at reframe-analysis time or lazily in `buildReframeContext`). `KeyAssumption` gains `source_assumption_id?: string`.
- `mergeAssumptionsIntoKeyAssumptions()` (context-chain.ts:506) propagates `id` → `source_assumption_id` instead of relying on text.
- `RecastStep` gains `validates_assumption_ids?: string[]` (set during recast generation when the AI is prompted to tag which assumption each step validates — see CLAUDE.md "Adding a New Field" checklist: type → store creator → defaults → Supabase column → all prompts → UI → handoff fns).
- DELETE the substring heuristics at agent-spec.ts:102-108 and prompt-chain.ts:150-153; replace with `step.validates_assumption_ids?.map(id => ctx.assumptionsById[id])`.
- If an older session lacks IDs, fall back to "no link shown" (defensive-data-access principle) — never guess.

### 1. New: `src/lib/ithaca-context.ts` (~180 lines)
```ts
export interface ProvenanceRef {
  phase: 'reframe' | 'recast' | 'rehearsal' | 'refinement';
  itemId: string;            // source item id
  field: string;             // e.g. 'reframed_question', 'key_assumptions.2'
  value: string;             // the source text, for the annotation panel
  user_modified?: boolean;
  timestamp?: string;
}
export interface AttributedField {
  text: string;
  provenance?: ProvenanceRef;   // omitted when truly unsourced
  tone?: 'normal' | 'reef';     // 'reef' = critical/unspoken risk → warm amber, not red dashboard
}
export interface IthacaContext {
  reframe: ReframeContext;
  recast: RecastContext;
  rehearsal: RehearsalContext;
  assumptionsById: Record<string, HiddenAssumption>;  // built once
}
export function buildIthacaContext(project: Project): IthacaContext  // composes the existing build*Context fns + indexes assumptions by id
```
This is the single source of truth all four generators read (kills the current duplication where each generator re-reads storage and re-derives context).

### 2. Brief → four-act ship's log (`src/lib/project-brief.ts`, rewrite section ordering)
Promote `voyageLogToMarkdown` from opt-in footer to the *spine*. New structure, all copy is final:
- `## ⚓ 출항 — 우리가 출발한 가설` (Departure): surface_task → reframed question → why_reframing_matters → the unverified assumptions as the open questions we set sail on.
- `## ⚠ 암초 — 항해 중 드러난 위험` (Reefs): rehearsal classified_risks (critical/unspoken) + each persona's top concern, each tagged with the assumption it threatens.
- `## ↻ 침로 수정 — 계획이 어떻게 바뀌었나` (Course-correction): refinement deltas + assumption verification changes ("출발 시 의심 → 리허설 후 확인됨"). Reuse waypoints (course_change / reef) from `voyageLogToMarkdown`.
- `## ⚑ 이타카 — 도착한 전략` (Ithaca): governing_idea, final step plan, total time, AI/human ratio, success metric.
Each act emits both markdown AND `AttributedField[]`. NO emoji glyphs beyond the existing nautical set (⚓↻⚠⚑) which are already the product's typographic marks — strip 🤖/🧠/🤝 actor emoji from strategist-facing render, replace with serif labels "AI · 사람 · 협업" in gold small-caps.

### 3. Brief render surface: `src/components/workspace/progressive/outputs/BriefShipLog.tsx` (NEW, ~220 lines)
Renders `AttributedField[]` acts in dawn-harbor mood:
- Container: `max-w-3xl`, `bg-[var(--surface)]` ivory, serif `var(--font-display)` for act headings, generous `space-y-8`.
- Each sourced field underlined with `decoration-dotted decoration-[var(--accent)]/40 hover:decoration-[var(--accent)]`. A small gold `(왜?)` lozenge after it.
- Clicking `(왜?)` opens `<ProvenanceNote>` — an inline editorial panel (NOT a graph), animating in with the canonical spring `transition={{ duration: 0.5, ease: [0.16,1,0.3,1] }}`. Content: phase label in gold small-caps ("리허설"), the source quote in serif italic, timestamp, and "✏️ 직접 수정함" if user_modified. Reuse `data-attribution-source` pattern from AttributedSection.
- `tone:'reef'` fields get a warm amber left-border `border-l-[3px] border-[var(--accent)]/50`, never red.

### 4. Prompt Chain footnote graft (`src/lib/prompt-chain.ts`)
Inside each generated prompt's `## 맥락` block, add one provenance footnote line built from the NEW id link:
`> 이 단계는 [재정의 가설 a2: "동남아 TAM 충분"]을 검증하고, [리허설 암초: CFO ROI 우려]에 대응합니다.`
Already-present `risk_if_false` injection (prompt-chain.ts:160) stays. The strategist-facing Prompt Chain card (optional render component `PromptChainCards.tsx`, reusing the BriefShipLog provenance note) shows this trail above each prompt; copy payload keeps it as a `>` blockquote so it survives paste into ChatGPT/Claude.

### 5. Abort-as-fork, STATIC text only (`src/lib/agent-spec.ts` + brief)
For any step whose `validates_assumption_ids` points at a doubtful/uncertain assumption with `risk_if_false`, emit a static contingency note — no modal, no runtime:
```yaml
    - step: 3
      validates_assumption: "a2: 동남아 TAM 충분"
      abort_condition: "TAM < $50M"
      if_abort: "여기서 멈추고 시장 선택으로 복귀 — 자동 진행 금지"
      contingency: "TAM 부족 시: TAM 확장 전략으로 전환"
```
This honors "hear but don't leap": it surfaces the fork for the human to judge, it does not automate the pivot.

### 6. Agent Spec = the ONE handoff bridge (`src/lib/agent-spec.ts` + `src/lib/agent-spec-graph.ts` NEW ~120 lines)
Only the Agent Spec gets destination variants, because it is the sanctioned descent to the execution layer:
- Existing YAML stays (now with id-based `validates_assumption`, `abort_condition`, `contingency`, `# provenance:` comments citing source phase).
- NEW `buildLangGraphJson(ctx)` → `{nodes, edges}` with `validates`, `abort_condition`, and `metadata.source_stage` per node; edges include the abort branch as a conditional edge. Pure function, JSON-serializable, downloaded via existing `downloadJson()`.
- UI: a small segmented control on the Agent Spec output ONLY — `[YAML (CrewAI)] [JSON (LangGraph)]`. No Cursor rules, no curl, no six-tool sniffing.

### 7. Checklist: keep static, add assumption-status column (`src/lib/checklist.ts`)
NO Supabase table, NO live sync (judge-rejected). Just enrich the existing markdown: each assumption checkbox shows its verification status carried from reframe/refinement (`확인됨`/`의심됨`/`미평가`) and a `↳ 검증 단계: Step N` line derived from the id link. This delivers 80% of the "live" feeling at 0 runtime cost.

### 8. FinalCard wiring (`src/components/workspace/progressive/FinalCard.tsx`)
- Evolve the existing single `withLog` checkbox into a two-state toggle: `[독자용 (깔끔)] [핸드오프용 (출처 포함)]`. Reader = current clean doc. Handoff = appends provenance footnotes + ship's log. Preserves the calm default (reader selected).
- Add the integrity summary line above ShareBar: `이 묶음에는 미확인 전제 {n}건 · 사람 판단 {m}건이 들어있습니다` — computed from ctx, one line, no modal.
- When the active output is the Brief, render `<BriefShipLog>` instead of `renderMd(content)`; other three keep markdown render for now (progressive enhancement).

### Token usage (all existing): `--accent` (gold) for provenance affordances, `--surface` ivory, `--font-display` serif, spring `cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)`, nautical glyphs ⚓↻⚠⚑. No new tokens, no tech-blue, no purple.
grafted_from_runners_up: From Live Execution Suite: abort/contingency as a fork, not a dead-end — rendered as STATIC `abort_condition`/`if_abort`/`contingency` text inside the Agent Spec and Brief, NOT as a live PivotModal/runtime (strips the runtime the judges unanimously rejected while keeping the 'hear but don't leap' insight).

From Executable Ithaca: per-destination variant generation (CrewAI YAML + LangGraph JSON via new agent-spec-graph.ts) confined to the Agent Spec ONLY, since it is the single sanctioned bridge to the execution layer — drops the rejected six-tool sniffing, cursor rules, and curl snippets.
From Executable Ithaca: the clean-vs-annotated export toggle, implemented as an evolution of FinalCard's existing 항해일지 checkbox into a [독자용]/[핸드오프용] switch that preserves the calm default.

From Executable Ithaca: the one-line handoff-integrity summary ('미확인 전제 N건 · 사람 판단 M건') before copy/share — a low-cost trust gesture, rendered as a single line, NOT the heavy confirmation modal the judges flagged as friction.

From both runners-up: replace the fragile substring assumption-linker with explicit stable assumption IDs threaded through the typed context chain (the craft judge's top buildability concern; makes provenance trustworthy).
acceptance_criteria: Stable IDs: every `HiddenAssumption` surfaced in outputs has a stable `id`; the Agent Spec's `validates_assumption` and the Prompt Chain footnote resolve via id lookup, not substring matching. Grep confirms `substring(0, 8)` / `substring(0, 10)` linker code is deleted from agent-spec.ts and prompt-chain.ts. Sessions missing IDs render with NO false link (verified by a test feeding legacy id-less data).

Brief renders as four labeled acts (출항/암초/침로 수정/이타카) sourced from reframe→rehearsal→refinement→recast respectively; the ship's log is the spine, not an opt-in footer. A test asserts all four act headings appear and each act's content derives from the correct phase.

Every sourced line in BriefShipLog exposes a `(왜?)` affordance that opens a ProvenanceNote showing {phase label, source quote, timestamp, user_modified flag} with the canonical spring easing; no node-graph is rendered on any strategist-facing surface (grep: no DAG/graph component imported by Brief/PromptChain/Checklist surfaces).

Prompt Chain prompts each contain a provenance footnote citing the originating reframe assumption (by id) and any rehearsal risk; the footnote survives clipboard copy as a markdown blockquote (snapshot test on `generatePromptChain` output).

Abort/contingency appears as STATIC `abort_condition` + `if_abort` + `contingency` text in the Agent Spec YAML for steps validating doubtful/uncertain assumptions; no execution runtime, store, modal, or Supabase table is introduced (grep: no useExecutionStore, no execution_logs/checklist_states migration, no Run-in-Claude handler).

Agent Spec offers exactly two destination variants — YAML (CrewAI) and JSON (LangGraph via buildLangGraphJson) — and this destination toggle exists on NO other output. LangGraph JSON validates as parseable JSON with nodes carrying `validates` + `metadata.source_stage`.

FinalCard shows a [독자용]/[핸드오프용] toggle defaulting to reader (clean), and a one-line integrity summary with correct counts of unverified assumptions and human-judgment steps; no confirmation modal is added.

Mood compliance: strategist-facing surfaces use only existing tokens (gold --accent, ivory --surface, serif --font-display, nautical glyphs); actor emoji 🤖/🧠/🤝 are replaced by serif 'AI·사람·협업' labels in Brief render; no tech-blue, purple, or red status pills introduced. Existing 1004 tests still pass; new tests cover id-linking, four-act Brief, and provenance resolution.
recommendation.sequencing_note: Depends on the Phase 0 typed context pipeline (context-chain.ts buildReframeContext/buildRecastContext/buildRehearsalContext), which already ships — so the IthacaContext composition is a thin layer, not new infrastructure. The hard prerequisite WITHIN this work is the stable-assumption-ID foundation fix (spec §0): it must land before the provenance features, because provenance built on the current substring linker would mislink and undermine the entire value proposition. That fix touches a typed field across the CLAUDE.md "add a field" checklist (types → store creator → defaults → Supabase column → recast/feedback/refine prompts → UI → handoff fns), so treat it as its own small PR that the recast-generation prompt must be updated to populate `validates_assumption_ids`. This surface does NOT depend on the ProgressiveFlow ~2670-line decomposition — the four generators are isolated pure functions and FinalCard is already extracted — but the new BriefShipLog/PromptChainCards components should live under a new `progressive/outputs/` folder to avoid growing ProgressiveFlow further, aligning with the broader decomposition direction. Sequence: (1) stable IDs + linker replacement, (2) IthacaContext + AttributedField generators, (3) BriefShipLog render + ProvenanceNote, (4) Prompt Chain footnotes + Checklist status column, (5) Agent Spec graph variant + FinalCard toggle/integrity line. Steps 3-5 are independently shippable progressive enhancements once 1-2 land.

concepts.concept_name: Editorial Print Design System for Argus
concepts.angle: editorial-print — Editorial print — like a beautifully typeset book/logbook: serif display, refined type scale & vertical rhythm, ink-on-cream, restrained gold
concepts.the_idea: Elevate Argus from "AI dashboard" to "premium editorial experience" by introducing a refined typographic hierarchy (serif display + robust serif body), a 8pt vertical rhythm grid, ink-on-cream color palette, and a reusable "Logbook Card" component that feels like pages from a captain's journal. Every interaction breathes like reading a beautifully printed book—generous whitespace, thoughtful contrast, slow motion, and a sense that thought matters.
key_moves: Strict 8pt vertical rhythm: all padding/margins are multiples of 8px (8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48). This creates visual coherence across all card, form, and step components and makes layouts 'tight but breathable'.

Serif-first display hierarchy: Replace generic headings with 'Noto Serif KR / Georgia' for all h1–h4 (display-xl/lg/md/sm). Body text stays sans-serif for readability, but display breaks the pattern deliberately.

Ink-on-cream palette refinement: Shift from the warm ivory (--bg: #f8f7f5) to a deeper, more yellow-cream tone (#f5f1e8, closer to aged parchment). Dark navy-charcoal text (#1a1a1a stays) creates stronger, more intentional contrast—'ink on parchment'.

Gold restraint (no saturation creep): Keep --accent at #96782e (unchanged) but reduce accent background opacity from /15 to /8 in borders and /6 in fills. Gold appears only as thin lines, highlight accents, or gradient text—never as oversaturated blocks.

Logbook Card reference component: A new, reusable card shape (rounded corners 12px, not 20px) with left-edge gold hairline border, serif subtitle, and generous 6px letterspace on labels. This becomes the 'page' in every step.

Paragraph spacing & measure: Set max-width for text blocks to ~65 chars (≈600px). Use line-height 1.7 (unchanged) but increase letter-spacing slightly on labels to 0.08em (from 0.12em—tighter feels more refined). Double line-height (3.4) between paragraphs.
Motion: Spring easing stays (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) but duration increases from 200ms to 280ms on micro-interactions. This makes the interface feel *deliberate*, not reactive.
Logbook texture: Add a subtle diagonal text-pattern overlay (3–5deg rotation, 60–80px pattern repeat) only to card backgrounds—not site-wide. Evokes aged paper without being distracting.
