concepts.tradeoffs:
**Traded-off for this angle:**

*Not covered (other angles handle these):*
- Deep technical agent orchestration and skill chains
- Single-user AI productivity superpowers
- Complex multi-step workflow automation

*Design constraints & risks:*
- Accuracy measurement requires user feedback ("was the CFO call right?"). If users skip the 10-second modal, entire loop breaks. Must make this a reflexive habit in onboarding.
- Outcome tracking is eventual; some voyages never get outcome data (exploratory projects, cancellations). System must gracefully handle ambiguity via confidence intervals in UI.
- Team boundaries create data silos; cross-team collective intelligence is lost at MVP. Anonymous global patterns could come later.
- Personas with sparse reactions won't have reliable accuracy scores; need sampling bias correction or confidence thresholds.
- Persona role assignments must be frictionless or adoption fails. Default-suggestion (by historical accuracy) with override is required.

*Technical costs:*
- 3 new Supabase tables + nightly pattern computation job. Manageable.
- Shareable URIs need expiration & optional access control (simple token scheme, context-aware, no auth wall).
- Real-time persona accuracy updates when feedback submitted; needs Supabase realtime subscription or polling.

*What users must do differently:*
- Share voyages explicitly (not automatic). Ask at export time.
- Provide feedback on persona accuracy (10-second modal, not a form).
- Invite team members by email. Require one-time accept, then automatic thereafter.

scores.judge_lens: Solo non-dev strategist whose alternative is asking ChatGPT directly. I weight visit two to three value with thin data, payoff under two minutes, and quiet first-mate tone over dashboard vibes. Ground truth I verified in code: navigator.ts, NavigatorStrip, NavigatorInline, and the patterns skill ALREADY render read-only personal coaching (tiered by session count, DQ sparkline, override and strategy patterns) sourced from useJudgmentStore.getUserPatterns, eval-engine, decision-quality, and judgment-vitality. ProgressiveSession has problem_text but NO asset, template, or outcome fields. useTeamStore exists (teams, members, invites, reviewInputs) but has no shared-voyage page or persona-accuracy-versus-outcome loop. This reality made Mirror cheap to ship, Living Assets a genuine greenfield build with cold start, and Collective both a build and a multiplayer-adoption bet the solo target user cannot satisfy in weeks one to three.

rankings.concept_name: Mirror Personal Judgment Atlas
rankings.note: Best value per effort for this lens. The moat the user FEELS is it-remembers-my-judgment, and the second-login growth card (acceptance 56 to 69 percent, you trust the reframes more) is exactly the under-two-minute scannable payoff that earns a return without homework. Feasibility is a 5 because roughly 70 percent already exists: getUserPatterns, the DQ sparkline, NavigatorStrip/NavigatorInline, and the patterns skill already extract and render personal patterns. So this is promoting an existing coaching layer into a first-class provenance-linked Mirror, not a 2-3k-line greenfield. Two deductions: it misrepresents reality by claiming the ledger is invisible today (it is already rendered, so the team should frame this as unify navigator plus patterns), and an always-visible right-rail chart dashboard with alert zones risks the exact generic AI-dashboard section 6 forbids; demote to calm one-insight first-mate observations opened on demand with n-under-5 uncertain labels.

rankings.concept_name: The Logbook as Knowledge Base Living Assets
rankings.note: Highest genuine-utility ceiling: Smart Defaults from your last similar voyage and you-have-tested-this-assumption-before make voyage six materially faster and sharper than a blank ChatGPT prompt, the most concrete smarter-every-use of the three, and chart-as-asset is straight from Philosophy 1.3. Cut by two hard problems: cold start (the headline features are empty until about five voyages, so they deliver zero value on the exact visits 2-3 that decide retention; the pioneering-this-territory fallback is a fig leaf) and feasibility 2 (ProgressiveSession has none of the needed fields, there is no outcome-recording pipeline, and similarity search plus three Supabase tables plus five new components is the biggest lift). Right move: graft the Related Voyages list plus Save-as-Template now and defer Smart Defaults until data exists. Tone is faithful but a Smart Defaults modal interrupting HeroFlow's calm near-empty opening screen risks violating section 3.1.

rankings.concept_name: Voyage Collective Team judgment charts
rankings.note: Wrong altitude for the stated solo non-dev user whose alternative is ChatGPT, not a team tool. Every value claim (team outperforms solo five to one, persona accuracy leaderboard, collective blind-spot cards) presupposes a team, five-plus shared voyages, and teammates reliably filling a ten-second accuracy modal, three adoption dependencies the target user cannot satisfy in weeks one to three, so visit-two value is near zero. Leaderboards and needs-work Dan-S 71 percent is competitive-dashboard energy section 6 warns against (fidelity 3, salvaged only by the on-DNA institutional-memory-of-how-we-judge idea). Feasibility 2: three tables, nightly jobs, realtime, context-aware shareable URIs beyond the current useTeamStore. This is a real Phase 6 cross-user network-effects concept, correct eventually but wrong as the retention mechanic that earns this user's second visit. Its one durable gift is the persona accuracy-versus-outcome calibration loop.

best_ideas_worth_grafting: Provenance links on every insight (Mirror's Found-in jump to the exact reframe item) grafted onto the EXISTING NavigatorStrip insights, which today state patterns without letting the user click back to the voyage where they were observed. This single move turns a stat into trust and teaching.

The second/third-login retention MOMENT framed as visible growth (acceptance 56 to 69 percent, you trust the reframes more), a scannable under-two-minute card wired to data navigator.ts already computes (DQ trend, override rate, vitality) rather than a new pipeline.

From Living Assets: the assumption-library badge in ReframeStep (you have questioned this before; last time it was refuted). Match the current hidden_assumption against past judgments and sessions and show a one-line precedent. Cheaper than full Smart Defaults and the most concrete smarter-every-use the user actually feels.

From Living Assets: Save-as-Template plus a Related Voyages list in the Logbook rail using domain plus keyword match v1 (no semantic search), giving returning users a head start without the five-voyage cold start of Smart Defaults.

From Living Assets: the outcome-to-assumption validation flow (this assumption was tested and held 80 percent of the time). Recording real outcomes is the missing data source that makes both Mirror's confidence-calibration patterns and any future asset library trustworthy; the highest-value plumbing investment.

From Voyage Collective: the persona accuracy-versus-outcome calibration loop (did the CFO's flagged risk actually materialize). Keep it as a SOLO feature first to sharpen the user's own rehearsal instinct and feed the Phase 3 PersonaBehaviorModel, aggregating to teams only later.

From Voyage Collective: the Argus-as-institutional-memory-of-how-we-judge idea, reframed away from leaderboards into the Mirror's own first-mate voice as a future shareable artifact instead of competitive scoring.

Cross-cutting craft rule for the winner: demote all surfaces from a persistent analytics dashboard to calm, on-demand, one-insight-at-a-time observations with n-under-5 uncertain honesty labels and I-notice-you-prefer-Y phrasing (observation not prescription), or the moat mechanic becomes the exact generic AI-dashboard section 6 forbids.

scores.judge_lens: Craft and feasibility on the real stack (Next 16, Tailwind v4, Zustand, framer-motion, Supabase, localStorage-first). I scored against what ALREADY exists in the repo. Decisive ground truth: a read-only judgment-intelligence layer already ships (useJudgmentStore.getUserPatterns, useAccuracyStore.getPersonaAccuracySummary, learning-health.assessLearningHealth with override_trend and tiers, judgment-vitality with analyzeVitalityTrend and buildProvenanceChain, signal-recorder, and a shipped /patterns skill); similarity.ts already exposes computeSimilarity and findSimilarItems (Korean-aware, already used for approval-to-plan and provenance); Logbook is already an aside rail reading checkpoint state_snapshots; useProgressiveStore uses an updateSession reducer with branch/checkpoint/snapshot machinery so pre-seeding a session is real new surface; useTeamStore has only members/invites/review-inputs, no cross-team accuracy and no shared no-auth route, and the codebase leans on RLS plus db.ts sanitization. I penalized net-new tables/jobs/routes that duplicate existing compute, O(n) work on component mount, no-auth share surfaces, and concepts that fight the calm single-screen solo-strategist DNA.

rankings.concept_name: Mirror (Personal Judgment Atlas)
rankings.note: Best fit to existing architecture; roughly 60-70 percent of the claimed work already ships: getUserPatterns (override rate, preferred actors), assessLearningHealth (override_trend plus tiers plus growth recommendations), analyzeVitalityTrend (improving/declining plus insight copy), getPersonaAccuracySummary (best/worst aspects = blind spots), and buildProvenanceChain (the Found-in click-through is literally already computed). The spec's own 2-3k-lines-plus-new-table estimate is overstated; the real build is a thin lib/mirror-aggregate.ts composing existing functions plus one Mirror.tsx (~300 lines) as a tab in the existing Logbook aside plus a useMirrorStore lazy cache. All source data is already localStorage-first. Faithful to philosophy: first-mate 'I notice you prefer Y' voice, gold bars on warm ivory, serif display, spring-grow charts, all expressible with current tokens and framer-motion. Knocked from 5 to 4 on feasibility only for two scope-creep riders to cut from v1: (a) the personal_patterns Supabase table is unnecessary since patterns are derivable read-only and persisting them invites staleness plus a migration, and (b) the opt-in compare-with-peers aggregate is a genuine privacy/data-liability surface against the RLS model. Lowest maintenance cost: a read-only view over data already recorded, matching the documented navigator/read-only pattern in judgment-vitality.ts.

rankings.concept_name: The Logbook as Knowledge Base (Living Assets)
rankings.note: Strongest moat-per-dollar IF descoped to v1 (Related Voyages rail plus Save-as-Template), which is nearly free thanks to already-shipped findSimilarItems and the Logbook reading state_snapshots; that v1 alone is a 4-5. Graded as a whole, the v2/v3 half pulls feasibility to 3: (1) getSmartDefaults injection via a new applySmartDefaults must pre-seed a session whose model is branch plus checkpoint plus state_snapshot, and createSession/updateSession does not take seeded analysis today, so this is error-prone (snapshot drift, branch invariants); (2) RelatedVoyagesSidebar's useEffect runs searchSimilarVoyages over ALL user sessions on every mount/problem_text change, an O(n) cosine pass in the render path that needs memoization plus a cap or the rail stops feeling instant; (3) assumption_library plus asset_tags are two new tables plus an anchor-time indexing step when the same tested-Nx-confirmed UX is derivable from buildProvenanceChain plus accuracy ratings; (4) the Smart Defaults modal at idle phase interrupts the section-3 calm-near-empty-screen one-question onboarding and should be a quiet inline chip. Korean copy already present, cold-start honestly acknowledged. Excellent ideas to graft, but as a standalone winner it sprawls across about 5 components plus 2 tables plus a store mutation and partly fights onboarding.

rankings.concept_name: Voyage Collective (Team judgment charts)
rankings.note: By far the heaviest lift and the worst architectural fit. Build cost: a new shared voyage route, 5 new components, 3 new Supabase tables, a nightly pattern-compute job, and realtime/polling for live accuracy, none of which exists (useTeamStore today is only teams/members/invites/review-inputs). Two hard red flags for this stack: (a) shareable URI not login-gated is a no-auth, token-guessable surface that runs directly against the documented security posture (RLS-enforced, all writes through db.ts sanitizeItem, team-visible data highest-priority for sanitization), a security-review liability rather than a feature; (b) the entire value loop depends on users reliably completing post-execution was-the-CFO-right and did-the-risk-materialize forms across many voyages and stakeholders, which the concept itself admits breaks if users skip the modal. Maintenance is highest (nightly job plus realtime plus cross-team silos plus sparse-persona sampling correction). Philosophy fidelity is lowest: ARGUS targets the solo non-developer strategist on a calm single screen, and a dense multi-pane team leaderboard with accuracy percentages, reminders, and comparison charts is exactly the generic AI dashboard the philosophy forbids. Salvage only the was-this-accurate micro-prompt and the strength/blind-spot copy structure, which graft into solo Mirror via the existing useAccuracyStore with zero team infrastructure.

best_ideas_worth_grafting: From Living Assets: the Related Voyages rail v1 is the cheapest high-value moat mechanic in any concept; findSimilarItems(session.problem_text, pastSessions) already exists and is Korean-aware. Add it as a section/tab INSIDE the existing Logbook aside (not a new always-on rail), gated at similarity >= 0.5, computed once in a useMemo keyed on problem_text so it never re-runs per render, and feed Mirror's Found-in provenance from it instead of building a parallel system.

From Living Assets: Save as Template in FinalCard.tsx is a clean contained win, just a boolean is_template plus optional domain/description on the existing ProgressiveSession with no new table; a saved template IS a crystallized judgment artifact that pairs with Mirror. Ship this and defer the assumption_library table and smart-defaults injection (the expensive, risky half that touches the branch/checkpoint/snapshot reducer).

From Living Assets: the You-have-tested-this-before / Tested-2x-(1-confirmed) assumption badge in ReframeStep is a strong concrete moment, but build it off the EXISTING buildProvenanceChain plus accuracy ratings keyed by computeSimilarity rather than a new assumption_library table; same UX, far less surface.

From Team Collective: the Was-this-accurate post-execution micro-prompt plus outcome-materialized capture is the right way to close Mirror's confidence-calibration loop (override then later validated); useAccuracyStore already stores accuracy_score and which_aspects_accurate, so reuse it and do NOT add a persona_accuracy_log table.

From Team Collective: the per-item strength/blind-spot/recommendation copy framing is good, applied SOLO via getPersonaAccuracySummary().bestAspects/worstAspects which already returns exactly this, making Mirror's blind-spot card concrete with zero new compute.

Keep Mirror's export-integration (a decision_log section appended on export) but route it through the existing lib/export.ts plus agent-spec.ts/checklist.ts pipeline rather than a bespoke YAML emitter, so all four Ithaca outputs stay single-source.

scores.judge_lens: Philosophy-fidelity guardian of the voyage DNA (§3 onboarding/context-carry, §6 동틀 녘의 항구 mood, §10 the 5 moments). I score how truly a retention concept extends the Odyssey/harness metaphor and serves moment #5 ("이 과정 자체가 AI 결과물보다 더 가치 있었네" / 메타 보정), and I penalize generic-AI-app drift hard: leaderboards, accuracy-% gamification, dashboard-card grids, cold benchmarking, and metaphor-as-decoration. The decisive question for "smarter every use": does the moat live in the USER'S judgment (해도가 곧 자산, §1.3) or does it drift into a SaaS analytics/scoreboard product? Grounded in code reality: useJudgmentStore + signal-recorder.ts + learning-health.ts (override-trend, learning_tier) + the existing /patterns skill already embody pattern-reflection with an observation-not-prescription tone — so a workspace mirror is a faithful extension, while team accuracy leaderboards are a net-new product surface with no voyage anchor.

rankings.concept_name: Mirror — Personal Judgment Atlas
rankings.note: Highest fidelity. This IS moment #5 (메타 보정) and §1.3 ('해도 자체가 지식 = 사용자의 여정') made visible — the moat lives in the USER'S accumulating judgment, exactly where philosophy says it must, never in 'smarter AI outputs' (which it explicitly cedes to ChatGPT). The tradeoffs section names this precisely. Feasibility is real, not aspirational: useJudgmentStore.addJudgment, signal-recorder.ts, useAccuracyStore, and learning-health.ts (override_trend, learning_tier, first-half/second-half comparison) already exist and already compute exactly the 'overrides decreasing = learning working' signal Mirror surfaces; the /patterns skill already does this reflection in the CLI with the right 'I notice you prefer Y' first-mate tone — Mirror ports a proven artifact into the workspace. DNA penalties to fix before build: (1) the 2nd-login modal copy 'This is the moat. This is why you return instead of ChatGPT' is 4th-wall-breaking product-marketing voice that violates §3.4's calm, suggestion-not-coercion tone and §6's editorial restraint — rewrite as logbook prose ('처음 출항과 지금, 항로를 읽는 눈이 이렇게 달라졌습니다'). (2) Naming drifts: 'Mirror / Judgment Compass / Navigator mode' stacks three non-voyage-or-mixed metaphors against §4.1 ('업무명과 항상 병기', max one metaphor per sentence) and §0 ('단어가 곧 기능'). Anchor it to existing vocabulary: 항해일지(logbook) already exists as the reflection surface — call it '항해일지 — 나의 항로 감각' rather than inventing Mirror/Compass. (3) ⚠️/📊/✨/🌍 emoji-card grid and 'Blind Spot alert zones' risk the generic AI-dashboard look §6 explicitly forbids; render as quiet serif observations on warm ivory with a single Graticule/gold sparkline, not alert chips. The 'Compare with peers' opt-in is the one genuinely off-DNA element — benchmarking against anonymized others is a SaaS-analytics instinct with no voyage anchor and contradicts the moat thesis (the point is YOUR ledger, not percentile rank); cut it or defer to Phase 6, don't ship it in the core surface.

rankings.concept_name: The Logbook as Knowledge Base: Asset Discovery, Pattern Recognition, and Smart Defaults
rankings.note: Strong fidelity — it is the literal product realization of §1.3's third chart-stage ('정밀 해도 = 독립 자산, 항해 너머의 가치') and ROADMAP v2.0 ('전체 해도 자체가 독립 문서'). 'Related Voyages', 'Save as Template', the assumption library tagged by 4축, and outcome-playback validating past assumptions all extend the voyage vocabulary honestly, and the Korean micro-copy ('이런 항해를 했던 것 같아요', '이 기반으로 시작') nails §4.1 metaphor+task pairing and the §6 editorial tone better than Mirror's English chrome. The deep DNA tension is with §3.1's calm near-empty-screen onboarding and the moment #1 promise: Smart Defaults pre-filling assumptions/personas/workflow on a NEW voyage risks short-circuiting '아, 내가 진짜 풀어야 할 문제가 이거였구나' — the product's reason to exist is to make you re-question, and auto-populating from a similar past voyage is a subtle path back toward 'just reuse the old answer' (the very first-Siren reflex §2.3 warns against). Mitigable by framing defaults as assumptions-to-RE-EXAMINE ('지난번엔 이렇게 가정했는데, 이번에도 같습니까?') rather than answers-to-accept, but as specced it leans accept. Feasibility is the lowest of the three: real value requires 5+ voyages of data (cold-start, which the spec admits) plus eventual semantic search/pgvector; the v1 keyword-match Related-Voyages sidebar is buildable now, but the headline Smart Defaults moment is gated on data the user doesn't have yet.

rankings.concept_name: Voyage Collective — Team judgment charts & shared persona accuracy
rankings.note: Lowest fidelity — this is where generic-SaaS drift is sharpest and my lens penalizes hardest. 'Persona Accuracy Leaderboard', 'team avg 82% ↑+6%', 'top performer / needs work', percentile scoreboards, and a multi-card analytics 'Judgment Canvas' are precisely the cold AI-dashboard / metrics-engagement aesthetic §6 says to AVOID, dressed with a thin voyage veneer. It also inverts the core thesis: §10's moments and §1 locate the moat in the SOLO user's eye that sees through the Siren's song (Argus the dog recognized one master) — converting that into inter-teammate accuracy ranking turns introspective 메타 보정 into competitive performance review, which can actively suppress the honest self-doubt the harness depends on (a teammate won't mark their own CFO call 'wrong' on a shared leaderboard). The few faithful kernels — institutional memory ('learn our decision culture by reviewing past voyages'), and outcome-tracking closing the loop on whether flagged risks materialized — are valuable but don't need leaderboards. Feasibility is also weakest: 3 new Supabase tables, nightly compute jobs, realtime subscriptions, shareable-URI access control, and an entire team layer that barely exists today (useTeamStore is 300 lines), all gated on multi-user feedback habits that the spec admits break the whole loop if skipped. Target-user mismatch too: the non-developer SOLO strategist (the stated user, real competitor = 'just ask ChatGPT') gets zero value until a team forms.

best_ideas_worth_grafting: From Living Assets: outcome-playback that flows a recorded outcome back to TAG past assumptions ('이 가정은 검증됐고 80% 들어맞았다') — graft this into Mirror so the judgment-ledger reflection shows not just 'you override X% of the time' but 'and when you overrode, you were later proven right Y% of the time' (closes the §3.4 메타 보정 loop with real-world validation, not just behavior counts).

From Living Assets: the assumption-library badge inside ReframeStep ('이 전제를 전에 4번 검증했습니다 — 그때 배운 것') — a low-cost, high-DNA way to make 'smarter every use' appear AT THE MOMENT of reframing (moment #1), not only in a separate reflection tab.
